text:
Alex (Support): FYI — ACME reported a big perf regression on the embeddings endpoint after last night's runtime push. Vectors/sec dropped from ~120k -> ~30k on their workload. tokens/sec looks steady at ~400k. No 5xxs, just slowness and queueing. They see GPU util pinned at 94-98%.

Priya (Eng-runtime): thanks. which cluster/region? any model variant change? did we flip any batching policy in the deploy?

Alex (Support): acme-prod-us-west1. They pinned model to rdx-embedding-1536:v2. No config changes on their side. We shipped runtime v3.14.0 last night (canary -> all).

DeployBot: deploy v3.14.0 to runtime-cluster-us-west1 completed by @ci (2025-11-24T02:45:12Z).

Marco (Eng-ML): quick thought: throughput drop with steady tokens/sec suggests per-call overhead or reduced effective batch size (vectors/sec down but tokens/sec same). Could be the batcher splitting into smaller micro-batches (more GPU invocations). Also check if we started falling back to CPU path for some requests (quantized kernels mismatch) — that would raise GPU util on some machines and cause longer tail.

Sam (Eng-SRE): running some queries now. Can someone share a repro payload and curl? I'll hit the same cluster.

Lina (Support): repro steps from ACME:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -d '{"model":"rdx-embedding-1536:v2","input":["text1","text2", ... 128 items]}'
```

They use batch_size=128; each input ~30 tokens. I ran locally against staging and saw vectors/sec ~32k.

Priya (Eng-runtime): Sam, run the batcher telemetry and queue depth for the period around the deploy. Example queries:

```
# prometheus-ish
sum(rate(runtime_batcher_effective_batch_size[5m])) by (node)
avg_over_time(runtime_queue_depth[5m])
```

Sam (Eng-SRE): pulled metrics for 02:30-03:30 UTC. Snippets:

```
# avg effective batch size across nodes
before deploy: 86.2
after deploy: 22.7
# queue depth (avg)
before: 12
after: 78
# GPU util (p99)
before: 72%
after: 97%
```

Sam (Eng-SRE): looks like the batcher is producing much smaller effective batches post-deploy; queue depth exploding while GPUs saturated. That matches vectors/sec drop but tokens/sec staying similar.

Priya (Eng-runtime): thanks — that points at a change in the batching heuristic or a new backpressure/timeout value. I remember we tweaked the 'max_wait_ms' and turned on per-request priority routing in v3.14.0. If max_wait got reduced aggressively we might flush tiny batches.

Marco (Eng-ML): also check model variant selection. If some requests routed to a quantized variant with slower decode/unpack path, effective throughput per GPU op could drop. But the big change in effective batch size suggests the batcher logic.

Alex (Support): ACME also reported occasional "dimension mismatch" warnings in logs for a small fraction (~0.3%) but no failing requests. Could that cause fallback?

Priya (Eng-runtime): dimension warnings can trigger a serialize-to-cpu path for the embedding head in some rare flows — that could make those tasks much heavier on CPU and stall the batcher while waiting. Need to grep runtime logs for the string "embedding dim mismatch" around the same windows.

Sam (Eng-SRE): grabbing logs...

```
# sample grep
grep -R "embedding dim mismatch" /var/log/runtime/2025-11-24/*.log | head
node-7.log:2025-11-24T02:52:13Z WARN embedding dim mismatch for req=abc123 (received 1536 expected 1024)
node-11.log:2025-11-24T02:52:18Z WARN embedding dim mismatch for req=def456 (received 1536 expected 1024)
```

Sam (Eng-SRE): interesting — some nodes are getting 1536 vectors where model expects 1024. That would cause a fallback or re-encode path. Why would we see 1024 expectation? Did a model variant with 1024 dim remain on some nodes?

Priya (Eng-runtime): oh. v3.14.0 introduced a model routing cache that maps model aliases to variants. I bet the cache had stale entries sending some requests to older 1024-dim variant while ACME pinned to 1536. Two things: (1) mismatched expected dims => runtime warns and may trigger CPU fallback, (2) batcher may group mixed-dim requests inefficiently.

Marco (Eng-ML): that explains the tiny effective batch sizes too — mixed-dim requests can't batch together, so batcher splits by dim which yields smaller groups. Plus CPU fallback path for mismatches stalls GPU pipeline, increasing queue depth and forcing more flushes.

Priya (Eng-runtime): action: roll back the model routing cache change and revert the max_wait_ms tweak in the batcher on prod. I'm going to stage a rollback to canary first.

DeployBot: rollback started for runtime v3.14.0 -> v3.13.9 on runtime-cluster-us-west1 by @Priya (2025-11-24T03:10:05Z).

Sam (Eng-SRE): monitoring metrics now.

QA-Bot: alert embeddings_throughput_drop fired at 2025-11-24T02:55:00Z (severity: P2).

Lina (Support): updated ACME: "we're investigating and running a rollback; will keep you posted."

Sam (Eng-SRE): after rollback (03:18 UTC):

```
# metrics post-rollback (03:18-03:30)
effective batch size: 82.9
queue depth avg: 10
vectors/sec: ~118k (back to baseline)
GPU util p99: ~74%
```

Alex (Support): ACME confirmed their throughput recovered to near normal. They also sent a log sample showing the dim mismatch entries you found.

Jae (Billing): ACME asked if they'd be billed for the degraded period — costs didn't spike on our end since GPUs were saturated but throughput low; we should offer a goodwill credit for their SLA hit. I'll coordinate with sales/legal.

Priya (Eng-runtime): root cause summary: two simultaneous changes in v3.14.0 — model routing cache + batcher max_wait_ms reduction — combined to cause mixed-dimension routing and aggressive flushes. Mixed-dim requests prevented effective batching and triggered CPU fallbacks for a small fraction, which cascaded to queue depth and GPU saturation.

Marco (Eng-ML): follow-ups:
- add stronger validation in routing cache to avoid stale variant mappings
- add unit/regression test that simulates mixed-dim flood and checks effective batch size
- health-check endpoint to surface per-dim allocation counts

Priya (Eng-runtime): operational follow-ups:
- revert permanently in next patch and roll a tested cache invalidation path
- add an alert that watches effective_batch_size drop and queue depth rise as a correlated signal
- create a runbook for "embeddings: batcher small-batch regression" with repro steps.

Alex (Support): I'll open a support case note and mark ACME incident follow-up. Filing a postmortem and linking the runbook.

Lina (Support): thanks all — will update ACME with rollback summary + next steps.

QA-Bot: scheduled regression test: embeddings_batching_regression in nightly suite starting 2025-11-25.

Priya (Eng-runtime): closing this thread; please ping if you see any residual anomalies.

Sam (Eng-SRE): closing monitoring loop, will create dashboard panels for effective_batch_size and per-dim routing counts.
